lines: A second order filter giving low pass, high pass, band pass and band stop versions of one input at the same time.
Sets the corner frequency of the filter, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 261.63Hz.
Sets the quality factor Q, 0.707 to 20; a Q of 20 peaks about 25dB, which is enough to clip the output.
Scales the level leaving the outputs, 0 to 100%, starting at 30%.
Attenuates the cutoff CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Attenuates the resonance CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Attenuates the drive CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Sets how much of the filtered signal reaches the outputs, 0 to 100%, starting at 100%.
Sets how much of the unfiltered input is mixed into the outputs, 0 to 100%, starting at nothing.
The audio to be filtered; sixteen channels are filtered separately.
Shifts the corner frequency by one octave per volt, scaled by its attenuverter.
Raises the quality factor Q; 10V adds the whole range of 20 with its attenuverter at maximum.
Raises the output level the drive knob sets; 10V adds the whole of it with its attenuverter at maximum.
The low pass version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
The high pass version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
The band pass version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
The band stop version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
Menu — Structure picks the biquad arithmetic used: Direct, Canonical, TransposeDirect or TransposeCanonical, the last of which stays steadiest under fast modulation.

TheWeb.notes: Params 0, 1 and 6 (the algorithm buttons and a boost/cut knob) are configured in the code but never placed on the panel and never read, so they are left untagged.

Sets the corner frequency of the filter, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 261.63Hz.
Sets the quality factor Q, 0.707 to 20: resonant peaking for the low pass and high pass, and the centre frequency divided by the -3dB bandwidth for the band pass and band stop.
Attenuates the cutoff CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Attenuates the resonance CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
The audio to be filtered; sixteen channels are filtered separately.

The band stop version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
A second order state variable filter modelled on the analogue circuit, giving low pass, high pass, band pass and band stop versions of one input.
Sets the corner frequency of the filter, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 261.63Hz.
Sets the quality factor Q, 0.707 to 20; with self oscillation switched on in the menu the filter oscillates at a Q of 20.
Sets the gain the filter applies to its output, -20dB to 20dB, flat at the centre.
Attenuates the cutoff CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Attenuates the resonance CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
The audio to be filtered; sixteen channels are filtered separately.
Shifts the corner frequency by one octave per volt, scaled by its attenuverter.
Raises the quality factor Q; 10V adds the whole range of 20 with its attenuverter at maximum.
Adds to the boost and cut directly, 20dB per volt, stopping at 20dB.
The low pass version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
The high pass version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
The band pass version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
The band stop version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
Nothing in the module reads this control; the boost CV is applied at a fixed 20dB per volt.
Menu — Enable Gain Compensation drops the level as Q rises, Match gain at Nyquist for LPF corrects the top end, Enable NLP adds non-linear processing, Enable Self Oscilation lets it ring at full Q.
LadyNina.notes: Param 6, the small knob under the Boost label whose tooltip reads Drive CV, is never read by the code: the boost and cut CV input is applied at a fixed 20dB per volt. It is on the panel and can be clicked, so it is tagged to a line saying it does nothing. Params 4 and 5 (Dry and Wet) are configured but not placed on the panel.

lines: Two resonators, which are band pass filters that can be made to peak very narrowly.
Switches between the two resonators: ResonA, a plain conjugate pole pair, and ResonB, the Smith-Angell design with a more symmetrical response.
Sets the corner frequency of the filter, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 261.63Hz.
Sets the -3dB bandwidth of the resonator, marked as a Q of 0.707 to 20.
Attenuates the cutoff CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Attenuates the quality CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.

Sets the shelving frequency, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 261.63Hz.
Sets the gain applied by the filter, -20dB to 20dB, flat at the centre.
Attenuates the cutoff CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Attenuates the boost and cut CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.

A third order Butterworth low pass ladder filter, built as a wave digital filter that models the resistors, capacitors and inductors of the analogue circuit.
Sets the cutoff frequency, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 261.63Hz.
Attenuates the cutoff CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
The audio to be filtered; sixteen channels are filtered separately.
Shifts the corner frequency by one octave per volt, scaled by its attenuverter.
The low passed audio.
Menu — Enable Warping corrects the mismatch between the analogue corner frequency and the digital one, which the component equations otherwise leave uncorrected.
An envelope detector: it follows the amplitude of an audio signal and puts out a control voltage that traces it.
Sets the rise time of the envelope, 1ms to 250ms, starting at 20ms.
Sets the fall time of the envelope, 1ms to 2 seconds, starting at 500ms.
Chooses what the detector measures: peak, mean-square or root-mean-square.
The audio whose amplitude is followed; sixteen channels are followed separately.
The envelope traced from the input.
Menu — Clamping holds the envelope at a ceiling of 1, and Output type switches it between a linear reading and a logarithmic one in dB.
An envelope follower driving the cutoff of a second order low pass filter, so that the louder the input the higher the filter opens.
Sets the cutoff the filter rests at while the input stays under the threshold, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 452Hz.
Sets the quality factor Q of the filter, 0.707 to 20.
Sets the rise time of the detector, 1ms to 250ms, starting at 20ms; the slope is measured in dB.
Sets the fall time of the detector, 1ms to 2 seconds, starting at 500ms; the slope is measured in dB.
Sets the level the detected envelope has to pass before the cutoff starts to move, -20dB to 0dB, starting at -6dB.
Multiplies how far the envelope has passed the threshold, 0.5 to 5, so the cutoff travels further and faster for the same input.
The audio to be filtered and followed; sixteen channels are treated separately.
The filtered audio.
Four voltage controlled low frequency oscillators with four ways of linking them, each giving a sine, triangle, square, rising ramp and falling ramp output.
Links the four oscillators: Free runs each on its own, Quad locks them to the first 90 degrees apart, Phase locks them to the first with a shift you set, Divide runs them at divisions of the first.
Sets the frequency of the first oscillator, 2 to the power of the knob value in Hz, so 1/128Hz to 128Hz.

Sets its oscillator's frequency from 1/128Hz to 128Hz in Free mode; in Quad it attenuates that oscillator, in Phase it shifts it 0 to 360 degrees, in Divide it divides the first oscillator by 2 to 32.
Scales the value its knob sets, 0 to 5V; with nothing patched the knob acts at its full value.
A trigger above 2V restarts that oscillator's cycle from zero.
A square wave from that oscillator, swinging between -5V and 5V.
A rising ramp from that oscillator, swinging between -5V and 5V.
A falling ramp from that oscillator, swinging between -5V and 5V.
A sine wave from that oscillator, swinging between -5V and 5V.
A triangle wave from that oscillator, swinging between -5V and 5V.
Note — each oscillator has a lamp blinking at its own rate, coloured red in Free mode, green in Quad, blue in Phase and white in Divide.
A stereo delay with three delay lines, 2 seconds of delay each, a shared feedback path and filters in that path.
Sets the delay time of the left line, 0 to 2 seconds, starting at 250ms.
Sets the delay time of the centre line, 0 to 2 seconds, starting at 250ms; the LCRDelay algorithm is the one that reads it.
Sets the delay time of the right line, 0 to 2 seconds, starting at 250ms.
Sets how much of the delayed signal is returned to the delay lines, 0 to 100%, starting at 50%.
Sets the right delay time as a proportion of the left one, 0 to 100%, starting at 50%.
Sets the level of the unprocessed input in the output, -60dB to 12dB, starting at -3dB.
Sets the level of the delayed signal in the output, -60dB to 12dB, starting at -3dB.
Steps through the four delay algorithms: Normal, a plain stereo delay; PingPong, which crosses the channels; LCRDelay, a left, centre and right delay with feedback on the centre only; and TapDelay.
Chooses where the right delay time comes from: Left+Ratio takes it from the left time scaled by the ratio, Left+Right takes each side from its own knob.
Sets the corner frequency of the low pass filter in the feedback path, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 452Hz.
Sets the corner frequency of the high pass filter in the feedback path, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 452Hz.
The left input to the delay.
The right input to the delay.
Measures the time between one trigger above 2V and the next, and sets all three delay times to that interval.
Scales the delay time its knob sets; 10V gives the whole of it and lower voltages shorten it in proportion.
Scales the ratio the knob sets; 10V gives the whole of it and lower voltages reduce it in proportion.
Scales the feedback the knob sets; 10V gives the whole of it and lower voltages reduce it in proportion.
Scales the wet level the knob sets; 10V gives the whole of it and lower voltages reduce it in proportion.
Scales the corner frequency of the feedback low pass; 10V gives the frequency its knob sets, lower voltages a lower one.
Scales the corner frequency of the feedback high pass; 10V gives the frequency its knob sets, lower voltages a lower one.
The left output of the delay.
The right output of the delay.
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the feedback percentage it is written into is overwritten by the Feedback knob on the next line of the code.
Menu — Enable Low Pass Filter and Enable High Pass Filter switch the two filters in the feedback path in and out, so they can be used alone, together or not at all.
CircularRide.notes: Input 8, the jack under the Dry knob, is read into the feedback percentage and that value is overwritten on the next line of the code, so the jack changes nothing; it is on the panel and can be patched, so it is tagged to a line saying it does nothing. Param 8 holds the algorithm shown on the display and is not a control on the panel.

lines: Three independent normalled switches, each choosing between two inputs and passing one of them to its output.
Reaches the output of its block only while the block's lower input has nothing patched into it.
Reaches the output of its block whenever a cable is in it, in place of the block's upper input.
Carries the block's lower input when that one is patched, and the block's upper input when it is not.
Note — sixteen channels pass through unchanged, and the channel count follows whichever input is in use.
DrillingHoles.notes: No families: the jacks carry whatever is patched into them, as with a mult. The module has no parameters.

lines: A stereo audio player that loads WAV, MP3 and FLAC files and plays the region between two markers.
Starts playing from the green start marker.
Stops playing and leaves the play line where it stands.
Winds the play line backwards through the sample while it is held down.
Winds the play line forwards through the sample while it is held down.
Unloads the file and opens a browser to pick another one.
Stops playing and returns the play line to the marker it started from.
Moves the green marker, where playing begins.
Moves the red marker, where playing ends; put it before the start marker and the sample plays backwards.
Places the sound between the two outputs, full left through centre to full right.
Sets the output level, 0dB at its default and 6dB at maximum.
Trims the playback rate about a tenth of a step either side of normal, so the sample plays a little slower or faster.
Draws the lower display over the region between the two markers, so a shorter and shorter stretch can be picked out.
Returns the lower display to the wider view it was drawn at before the last zoom.
Moves the panning; 5V drives it fully to one side and -5V fully to the other, added to the knob setting.
Rising past 2V starts playing, and falling back below 0.1V pauses.
The left channel of the player.
The right channel of the player.
Menu — Panningtype chooses Simple or Constant Power panning, PlayMode chooses Single, Repeat or PingPong, and Select Audio File loads a file without using the eject button.
A phase modulation oscillator with a frequency ratio drawn from tuning tables, through-zero FM, feedback, a wave shaper and a VCA.
Sets the frequency as a ratio of the pitch at V/OCT, a ratio of 1.00 giving C4 at 0V; the stepping in force governs which ratios the knob can reach.
Adds to the ratio the knob sets, over a 0-10V range; bipolar signals work, and each channel can take its own ratio.
Steps through the three waveforms: sine, wave folder, and a triangle that blends to saw.
Steps through the tables of ratios: none, legacy, Legacy+Sub, Octaves, Digitone, DX11 and DX7.
Opens the VCA from silence to full as a bias, with any modulation added on top of the setting.
Drives the VCA, 0-10V; the polarity switch sets whether the voltage opens the VCA or closes it.
Chooses the response of the VCA to its modulation: linear, or a fourth-power curve.
Chooses whether the voltage driving the VCA opens it from the knob setting or closes it from there.
Shifts the pitch of the whole oscillator, -12 to +12 semitones.
Sets the amount of through-zero frequency modulation taken from the LFM input, 0 to 100%.
Scales the through-zero FM amount, 0-10V between nothing and the amount the Depth knob sets.
Attenuates the FM input, 0 to 100%.
A bipolar voltage added to the pitch, scaled by the FM knob; good for vibrato and pitch envelopes.
Sets how much of the output is fed back into the oscillator's own phase, 0 to 100%, from a slight change of timbre to noise.
Scales the feedback amount, 0-10V between nothing and the amount the Fdbk knob sets.
Sets the shaping amount, 0 to 100%: it drives the folder on the wave folder waveform and blends triangle to saw on the third; it changes nothing on the sine.
Scales the shaping amount, 0-10V between nothing and the amount the Shape knob sets.
The audio used as the modulator for through-zero frequency modulation.
Sets the pitch, one volt per octave.
Hard syncs the oscillator to the signal patched here, for classic synced lead sounds.
The oscillator's audio, up to 5V either side at a fully open VCA.
Note — every input is polyphonic, and a single-channel modulation patched into any of them acts on all the channels at once.
Note — a file called RPJ.json in the VCV user folder adds your own tables of ratios to the stepping list; a Pigeon Plink added after it is written picks them up.
PigeonPlink.notes: Param 9, the output level, is placed at the same spot as the Fdbk knob and is covered by it, and the value it holds is overwritten by the VCA calculation, so it is left untagged. Params 5, 7 and 12 are configured but never placed on the panel.

lines: A chaos generator built from four double pendulums, each giving the x and y position of its first joint and the angle of its upper arm.
Sets how fast the pendulums run, 1 to 10 times the base rate.
Attenuates the speed CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Sets the mass of both weights on every pendulum, 0.1 to 10.
Attenuates the mass CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Sets the length of the pendulum arms, a tenth of full scale to full scale, which scales how far the x and y outputs swing.
Attenuates the length CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Lifts the x and y outputs by 5V so that they stay positive, and lights red while it is on.
Sets all four pendulums to a fresh random starting position.
Adds to the speed, scaled by its attenuverter.
Adds to the arm length, scaled by its attenuverter.
Adds to the mass, scaled by its attenuverter.
The horizontal position of that pendulum's first joint, -5V to 5V at full arm length.
The vertical position of that pendulum's first joint, -5V to 5V at full arm length.
The angle of that pendulum's upper arm in radians, divided by 18 to bring it into a usable voltage.
Menu — Number of Pendulums sets how many of the four are running, from 1 to 4.
The display for Genie, drawing its four double pendulums; it goes immediately to the right of the Genie it belongs to.
Sets how many past positions are drawn behind each weight, 1 to 100, each one fading as it ages, despite the maker's manual giving that to THICK.
Sets how often a new position is added to those trails, from one draw in five to every draw, despite the maker's manual giving that to SWARM.
Moves that pendulum left and right on the display; dragging its root weight with the mouse does the same.
Moves that pendulum up and down on the display; dragging its root weight with the mouse does the same.
The horizontal position of a shape drawn on the display in place of that pendulum; the Y jack of the same row has to be patched as well.
The vertical position of a shape drawn on the display in place of that pendulum; the X jack of the same row has to be patched as well.
Menu — Draw Lines between Nodes joins the weights with lines, and a colour slider is given for the root, for each of the four nodes and for the lines.
GenieExpander.notes: Param 0 is labelled SWARM on the panel and tooltipped Swarm length, and param 1 is labelled THICK and tooltipped Swarm thickness. In the code param 0 sets the number of past positions held in each trail and param 1 sets how often a position is added to it. The maker's documentation describes the pair the other way round, so each line carries a clause naming the conflict.
